note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every claim below comes from a named source in `sources`. Charlotte is the first city in this directory whose operator publishes no court count at all. Mecklenburg County lists individual numbered courts instead, and the counts here are the number of distinct court numbers it names at each park. Where the county is silent, the note says so rather than filling the gap.

slots.parking:
Mecklenburg County publishes one sentence about parking across its whole park system, and it is a warning: local parks, meaning neighbourhood parks, "do not typically have parking or restroom features as these locations are small to medium parks that are meant to provide open space for residents near their homes". None of the five pickleball parks here is classified as a neighbourhood park, so the warning most likely does not apply to them. Most likely is not a fact, and no venue here records anything about parking or restrooms.

The county publishes no capacity, time limit, permit requirement or fee for parking at any of the five.
slots.peak_hours:
Charlotte is the only city in this directory where the operator splits each park's courts between bookable and not, court by court. Mecklenburg County says that "Some courts can be reserved for a small fee" and that "Any courts not listed are non-reservable and open to the public on a first come, first serve basis".

Clarks Creek reserves courts 1 to 5 and leaves 6, 7 and 8 open. Clanton reserves 1 to 4 and leaves 5 and 6. Freedom reserves 11, 12, 14 and 15 and leaves 13 and 16. Martin Luther King Jr. reserves 2, 3, 5 and 6 and leaves 1 and 4. Beatty reserves 2 and 3 and leaves 1. Every park keeps some courts back. At Beatty that means competing for a single court.

The county publishes no opening hours for any of them. It says local park courts "are always open for play", which is a statement about access rather than a timetable. It publishes no lighting information at all, so every venue here reads "Not stated" on lights.
slots.surface_condition: Nothing at all. Mecklenburg County publishes no surface material, no condition and no resurfacing date for any of the five parks, so every Charlotte venue reads "Not stated" on surface. What it does state is each park's size class. Freedom Park and Colonel Francis J. Beatty Park are Regional parks, the largest category, and the other three are Community parks. All five are recorded as Developed rather than planned or undeveloped.
slots.local_scene:
The Mecklenburg County Park and Recreation Department runs 290 parks and facilities across more than 23,000 acres. What makes Charlotte distinctive in this directory is not scale but bookkeeping: it is the only operator that identifies courts individually, by number, and tells you which of them can be reserved.

At Freedom Park the pickleball courts are numbered 11 to 16, because courts 1 to 10 at the same park are tennis courts, listed separately higher up the same page. The county runs one numbering series across both sports at that site.

The same county page lists six Hybrid Courts each at Latta Park and Tuckaseegee Park under their own heading, and never says what a hybrid court is. Those twelve courts are not published here until the county defines the term. Reservations cost "a small fee" with no price named, so every venue reads "Not stated" on cost.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts
best_for.text: Clarks Creek Park, with eight, the largest pickleball site we list in Charlotte, in the north of the city off Hucks Road. Courts 1 to 5 are reservable and 6, 7 and 8 are always open play. Do not confuse it with Clarks Creek Nature Preserve directly across the road, or Clarks Creek Greenway Park on Mallard Creek Road; the county's parks layer holds all three as separate records.

best_for.heading: Best odds without a booking
best_for.text: Again Clarks Creek: three of its eight courts are permanently open play, more than any other Charlotte park. Clanton, Freedom and Martin Luther King Jr. each keep two back, and Colonel Francis J. Beatty Park keeps exactly one of its three.

best_for.heading: Best known park on the list
best_for.text: Freedom Park, one of the county's Regional parks and a Charlotte landmark in its own right. Six pickleball courts, numbered 11 to 16. Four are reservable and two (13 and 16) are always open play. The county publishes nothing about lighting, surface or hours for them.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Charlotte have?
faqs.a: 29 across five Mecklenburg County parks: eight at Clarks Creek Park, six each at Clanton Park, Freedom Park and Martin Luther King Jr. Park, and three at Colonel Francis J. Beatty Park. The county also lists six "hybrid" courts each at Latta Park and Tuckaseegee Park, which are not published here because it never says what a hybrid court is.

faqs.q: Can I reserve a court in Charlotte?
faqs.a: At most of them, yes. Nineteen of the 29 courts are reservable for what the county calls "a small fee"; the other ten are always open play on a first-come, first-served basis. Every park keeps at least one court back for drop-in play. The county does not publish what the fee is, so cost is recorded as not stated.

faqs.q: Is Colonel Francis J. Beatty Park in Charlotte or Matthews?
faqs.a: Charlotte, though the records disagree. Its postcode is 28105, a Matthews mailing ZIP, while the City of Charlotte parks layer labels its city as Charlotte. The US Census geocoder places the park's published coordinates inside the incorporated place of Charlotte, in Mecklenburg County.

sources.evidence: "Local park courts are always open for play. Local parks (neighborhood parks) do not typically have parking or restroom features as these locations are small to medium parks that are meant to provide open space for residents near their homes." "Some courts can be reserved for a small fee. Any courts not listed are non-reservable and open to the public on a first come, first serve basis." Reservable Pickleball Courts: Clarks Creek Park Courts 1-5; Clanton Park Courts 1-4; Colonel Francis J. Beatty Park Courts 2&3; Freedom Park Courts 11, 12, 14, 15; MLK Park Courts 2,3,5,6. Open Play Pickleball Courts: Clarks Creek Park Courts 6-8; Clanton Park Courts 5&6; Colonel Francis J. Beatty Park Court 1; Freedom Park Courts 13&16; MLK Park Courts 1&4. Hybrid Courts, listed under a separate heading and undefined: Latta Park Courts 1-4 reservable and 5&6 open play; Tuckaseegee Park the same. Freedom Park also appears under Tennis Courts with Courts 1-6 reservable and 7-10 open play. No lighting, surface, hours or fee amount is published.

"The Mecklenburg County Park and Recreation Department is home to 290 parks and facilities located on more than 23,000 acres of parkland throughout Mecklenburg County." Closure notice at the time of reading: "The large playground in Nevin Park is closed until further notice." No court-level condition or closure information is published.
